decisions.reason: The published Gaussian Definition supplies existence but explicitly defers uniqueness. Its characteristic-function lemma proves uniqueness under AC for every positive-semidefinite scale, including singular scales. Adding that established supplier to deps licenses the uniquely specified Gaussian factors, their finite product, and the continuous outer-product pushforward without changing the Definition.

The submitted MLE objection is not upheld: the Definition calls M a covariance candidate and defers its MLE property, while the actual likelihood theorem assumes n>p and proves M positive definite almost surely before optimization. Review nevertheless confirms the same fatal missing Gaussian-uniqueness dependency as in def-wishart-law: the parameter-indexed product P_mu,Sigma requires a uniquely specified normal law, whereas its cited Gaussian Definition explicitly defers uniqueness. Added the established characteristic-function/uniqueness lemma to deps; no MLE claim or Definition was weakened.

F2 and F3 imported a random-statistic F law and exact-size guarantee without the iid Gaussian experiment, positive-definite covariance or AC required by their actual suppliers. Fixed vectors alone give only arithmetic, not a null law or a test size. Added the reference experiment and AC to Example/Given, restored every supplier hypothesis in F2/F3, and retained n=4>p=2 and the exact strict cutoff.

reviews.reason: Checked the full Gaussian uniqueness lemma: equality of transforms identifies all scalar projections and Cramer-Wold identifies the vector law, including singular covariance. Probability factors are sigma-finite; iteration of the product theorem gives a probability product; the finite polynomial outer-product map is continuous and Borel under AC. Added only the missing uniqueness dependency; the Definition, p,m>=1, singular support and choice scope are unchanged.

Checked n>=2 makes both covariance denominators positive and the mean/scatter maps polynomial, hence continuous; the parameter covariance is positive definite, while observed M may be singular and is only called a candidate. The likelihood supplier's step 3.1 establishes the MLE on the almost-sure positive-definite event under n>p. Added the Gaussian uniqueness lemma to license the parameter-indexed product law. Sampling/vector units, fixed parameters, identity observation map, AC and the complete Definition remain unchanged.

Checked the complete Hotelling theorem and exact-test corollary: AC, iid normal vector observations, positive-definite population covariance, n>p and the mean null give the F law and common size alpha. The repaired example supplies this reference model while computing a fixed observation. Directly verified mean zero, R=2I_2, S=2I_2/3, inverse=3I_2/2, T^2=12, factor 1/3 and scaled value 4. The unique F(2,2) quantile and strict inequality remain valid for every alpha in (0,1).
